COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
C482 No.715 of 2023
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Ramji Shrivastava, learned counsel for 
the applicant.
Mr. A.K. Sah, learned Deputy Advocate 
General along with Mr. Mamta Joshi, learned 
Brief Holder for the State.
Mr. B.D. Jha, Ms. Preeti Jha and Ms. 
Priyanka, learned counsel for the private 
respondent.
This Court vide its order of 17.04.2023 had 
issued notice to the private respondent in order 
to call upon the opposite party to make an effort 
for mediation.
The applicant has put in appearance in 
compliance of the earlier order.
Respondent no.2 has put in appearance 
through Mr. B.D. Jha, Ms. Preeti Jha as well as 
Ms. Priyanka Jha, learned counsel. 
Mr. B.D. Jha, learned counsel, who 
appears for the respondent, submits that 
instead of venturing into the settlement, he 
want to file a detailed counter affidavit to the 
C482 application.
He prays that he may be granted six weeks’  time.
His prayer is accepted.
He may file his counter affidavit within a 
period of six weeks from today.
Till the next date of listing, further 
proceedings of Criminal Case Non.554 of 2021, 
“State Vs. Aditya Prakash” pending 
consideration before the court of learned Vth 
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dehradun 
would be kept in abeyance.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 22.05.2023 Sukhbant

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
20.05.2024 C482 No. 715 of 2023
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Nishant Krishna Adhikari, learned 
counsel for the applicant, Mr. V.S. Pal, learned 
AGA for the State, Mr. B.D. Jha, learned counsel 
for the respondent through V.C.
2. Pursuant to the previous order, the 
applicant is present in Court physically and the 
respondent No. 2 appeared through V.C. with 
her minor daughter and mother.
3. The applicant is a practicing lawyer in 
Dehradun and respondent No. 2 is also doing 
LLB degree and as such both of them are from 
same legal fraternity. On the previous date, this 
Court observed that since both of them are 
from the same legal fraternity, therefore, they 
are the best persons to resolve their disputes.
4. Today, on interaction with the 
present applicant, who is present in Court,
submits that respondent No. 2 is not facilitating 
to talk with the daughter. On interaction, she 
informed that she is living in her in-law’s house.
5. The applicant has given his mobile 
No. i.e. 9760340412. The respondent No. 2 is  directed to facilitate her daughter to talk with 
the applicant regularly. The respondent No. 2 
has also given her mobile No. i.e. 9193333445. 
Both the parties are directed to talk each other 
through their mobile numbers and respondent 
No. 2 is also directed to facilitate her daughter 
to talk with her father i.e. the applicant.
6. Put up this matter on 24.06.2024. 
7. On that day, both the parties shall 
remain present in Court.
8. In the meantime, the applicant shall 
pay a sum of Rs. 20,000/- to the respondent 
/wife.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 20.05.2024
Mahinder/

C482 No. 715 of 2024
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel for 
the applicant.
2. Mr. V.S. Pal, learned A.G.A. and Ms. 
Sandeep Sharma, learned Brief Holder for 
the State.
3. Mr. B.D. Jha, learned counsel for the 
complainant (through V.C.)
4. Pursuant to the previous order dated 
24.06.2024, both the applicant and 
respondent/complainant are present. Their 
daughter Aradhya Sharma, is also present 
and she was interacted by one of lady staff 
as well as by Ms. Shruti Joshi, Advocate for 
half an hour.
5. After interaction with the daughter this 
Court is of the view that last chance should 
be given to the applicant/husband to get in 
touch with the daughter as well as wife 
happily and this opportunity is being given 
to the applicant to settle the matrimonial 
life.
6. Put up this matter on 20.08.2024. On 
that day both the applicant, complainant as
well as their daughter shall remain present 
in Court. It is also directed that both the 
parties particularly the applicant/husband 
shall comply in strict sense the directions 
issued by order dated 20.05.2024.
7. Interim order shall continue till the 
next date of listing.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
